text:
Leaving Tokyo at noon for Kamakura?
Hase's temples stop letting people in around 16:30,
almost exactly when the winter sun sets over the sea.
Plan it in that order 👇

👉 Which big sight is still open at 8 p.m.? Guess:
https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset

🚆 Getting there, with no change
The 11:36 Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station
reaches Kamakura at 12:33. The JR Pass covers it.

🛕 First, the temples
Take the green Enoden two stops to Hase (¥200).
The Great Buddha lets people in until 16:45 in winter.
At Hasedera, five minutes away, last entry is 16:30.

🌅 Then the sunset
Two more stops to Inamuragasaki,
then an 8-minute walk to the cape.
On windy days from December to February,
Mount Fuji often joins in.

⛩️ Then the shrine
Back to Kamakura (¥220), then 10 minutes on foot.
Tsurugaoka Hachimangu's gates stay open until 20:00.

💭 Our take
Don't squeeze in Kita-Kamakura as well.
One area, three short rides and a sunset
beat six temples at a jog.

👉 Why we'd save the biggest shrine for last:
https://japanbystation.com/kamakura-from-noon-temples-or-sunset

if you could only pick one, which would it be?
